title: Pictograms and Tally Charts
seo_title: Pictograms – Primary 2 Mathematics Worksheets with Answers (NERDC)
standard_text: Collect data using tally marks; read and make pictograms and block graphs; answer questions from the data. (summary of the NERDC Primary 2 Mathematics curriculum)
meta_desc: Free Primary 2 maths worksheets on data: tally marks, pictograms where one picture stands for one or more things, block graphs and data questions. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: One picture can stand for 2 or more
body_html:
How to think about it

  • A tally mark | stands for one thing. Five is drawn as |||| with a line across.
  • A pictogram uses pictures. The key tells what one picture means.
  • Count and compare: which has the most? which has the least?

Examples

Example

Key: 1 picture = 2 children. Rice has 3 pictures

3 × 2

Answer: 6 children

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Forgetting the keyUse the key.
Counting tallies one by oneCount in fives.
Reading the wrong rowUse your finger to follow the row.

items.q: What number does this tally show?
items.e: Four lines with one line across make a group of 5. 1 group of 5. Count in 5s: 5. So it is 5.

items.q: What number does this tally show?
items.e: Four lines with one line across make a group of 5. 1 group of 5 and 2 more. Count in 5s: 5, then 6, 7. So it is 7.

items.q: What number does this tally show?
items.e: Four lines with one line across make a group of 5. 2 groups of 5. Count in 5s: 5, 10. So it is 10.

items.q: What number does this tally show?
items.e: Four lines with one line across make a group of 5. 2 groups of 5 and 3 more. Count in 5s: 5, 10, then 11, 12, 13. So it is 13.

items.q: What number does this tally show?
items.e: Four lines with one line across make a group of 5. 3 groups of 5 and 3 more. Count in 5s: 5, 10, 15, then 16, 17, 18. So it is 18.

items.q: How many children have a hamster?
items.e: Find the Hamster row. It has 1 group of 5 and 3 more. Count in 5s: 5, then 6, 7, 8. So it is 8.

items.q: How many children chose tag?
items.e: Find the Tag row. It has 1 group of 5 and 3 more. Count in 5s: 5, then 6, 7, 8. So it is 8.

items.q: How many spiders were found?
items.e: Find the Spider row. It has 1 group of 5 and 3 more. Count in 5s: 5, then 6, 7, 8. So it is 8.

items.q: How many silver cars went past?
items.e: Find the Silver row. It has 1 group of 5 and 1 more. Count in 5s: 5, then 6. So it is 6.

items.q: Which row shows 17 children?
items.e: 17 is 5 + 5 + 5 + 2. The Yellow row has 3 groups of 5 and 2 more. Count in 5s: 5, 10, 15, then 16, 17. So it is 17.

items.q: Which row shows 15 birds?
items.e: 15 is 5 + 5 + 5. The Pigeon row has 3 groups of 5. Count in 5s: 5, 10, 15. So it is 15.

items.q: Which game is the most popular?
items.e: Count every row: Skipping 5, Football 2, Hopscotch 7, Tag 8. The biggest number is 8, for Tag.

items.q: Which colour of car went past the least?
items.e: Count every row: White 18, Silver 6, Black 12, Blue 11. The smallest number is 6, for Silver.

items.q: Which tally shows 8?
items.e: C is right: 1 group of 5 and 3 more. Count in 5s: 5, then 6, 7, 8. So it is 8. A: it has one mark too many; B: the groups have five upright lines and a line across, so each group is 6; D: it has one mark too few.

items.q: Which tally shows 13?
items.e: A is right: 2 groups of 5 and 3 more. Count in 5s: 5, 10, then 11, 12, 13. So it is 13. B: the groups have no line across, so they are hard to count in 5s; C: it has one mark too few; D: the groups have five upright lines and a line across, so each group is 6.

items.q: Which tally shows 17?
items.e: D is right: 3 groups of 5 and 2 more. Count in 5s: 5, 10, 15, then 16, 17. So it is 17. A: the groups have five upright lines and a line across, so each group is 6; B: it has one mark too many; C: the groups have no line across, so they are hard to count in 5s.

items.q: How many more children have a hamster than a dog?
items.e: Hamster: 8. Dog: 6. How many more means find the difference: 8 − 6 = 2.

items.q: How many fewer snails than worms were found?
items.e: Worm: 11. Snail: 6. How many fewer means find the difference: 11 − 6 = 5.

items.q: How many children voted altogether?
items.e: Count every row: Yellow 17, Red 4, Green 6, Purple 16. Then add: 17 + 4 + 6 + 16 = 43.

items.q: How many birds were seen altogether?
items.e: Count every row: Sparrow 7, Pigeon 15, Robin 10, Blue tit 14. Then add: 7 + 15 + 10 + 14 = 46.

items.q: How many children chose vanilla?
items.e: Each circle = 1 child. Count the circles in the Vanilla row: 4 children.
Each star = 1 child. Count the stars in the Pear row: 3 children.

items.q: How many children have a fish?
items.e: Each square = 1 child. Count the squares in the Fish row: 9 children.
Each heart = 1 car. Count the hearts in the Blue row: 7 cars.

items.q: How many children chose skipping?
items.e: Each circle = 1 child. Count the circles in the Skipping row: 4 children.
Each star = 1 minibeast. Count the stars in the Ladybird row: 7 ladybirds.

items.q: Which row shows 4 children?
items.e: Each square = 1 child. Look for the row with 4 squares. That is Bus.
Each heart = 1 bird. Look for the row with 5 hearts. That is Blue tit.

items.q: Which colour is the most popular?
items.e: Each circle = 1 child. The Red row has the most circles: 9.
Each star = 1 child. The Scooter row has the most stars: 6.

items.q: Which flavour is the least popular?
items.e: Each square = 1 child. The Mint row has the fewest squares: 2.
Each heart = 1 child. The Apple row has the fewest hearts: 3.

items.q: How many more snails than worms were found?
items.e: Each circle = 1 minibeast. Snail: 3. Worm: 1. How many more means find the difference: 3 − 1 = 2.
Each star = 1 bird. Pigeon: 7. Sparrow: 1. How many fewer means find the difference: 7 − 1 = 6.

items.q: How many more red cars than blue cars went past?
items.e: Each square = 1 car. Red: 7. Blue: 3. How many more means find the difference: 7 − 3 = 4.
Each heart = 1 child. Dog: 3. Hamster: 1. Add them: 3 + 1 = 4.

items.q: How many children chose football or hopscotch?
items.e: Each circle = 1 child. Football: 4. Hopscotch: 8. Add them: 4 + 8 = 12.
Each star = 1 child. Purple: 8. Yellow: 1. Add them: 8 + 1 = 9.

items.q: How many children voted altogether?
items.e: Each square = 1 child. Count every row: Banana 7, Orange 2, Pear 3, Grapes 4. Add them: 7 + 2 + 3 + 4 = 16.
Each heart = 1 child. Count every row: Hamster 3, Cat 6, Rabbit 9, Dog 7. Add them: 3 + 6 + 9 + 7 = 25.

items.q: How many children chose mint?
items.e: Look at the key: each circle = 2 children, so half a circle = 1. The Mint row has 8 circles. Count in 2s: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16. So it is 16 children.
Look at the key: each star = 5 children. The Apple row has 7 stars. Count in 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35. So it is 35 children.

items.q: How many children chose blue?
items.e: Look at the key: each square = 10 children. The Blue row has 3 squares. Count in 10s: 10, 20, 30. So it is 30 children.

items.q: How many children have a rabbit?
items.e: Look at the key: each circle = 2 children, so half a circle = 1. The Rabbit row has 2 circles. Count in 2s: 2, 4. So it is 4 children.
Look at the key: each star = 2 birds, so half a star = 1. The Blackbird row has 7 stars and half a star. Count in 2s: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, then 1 more for the half. So it is 15 blackbirds.
Look at the key: each star = 5 children. The Tag row has 3 stars. Count in 5s: 5, 10, 15. So it is 15 children.

items.q: How many children walk to school?
items.e: Look at the key: each square = 10 children. The Walk row has 7 squares. Count in 10s: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70. So it is 70 children.
Look at the key: each star = 2 minibeasts, so half a star = 1. The Worm row has 3 stars and half a star. Count in 2s: 2, 4, 6, then 1 more for the half. So it is 7 worms.

items.q: Each square stands for 5 children. 20 children chose tag. How many squares go in the Tag row?
items.e: Count in 5s until you reach 20: 5, 10, 15, 20. That is 4 steps, so draw 4 squares, not 20.

items.q: Each circle stands for 10 children. 60 children walk to school. How many circles go in the Walk row?
items.e: Count in 10s until you reach 60: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60. That is 6 steps, so draw 6 circles, not 60.

items.q: How many children chose strawberry?
items.e: Look at the key: each square = 10 children. The Strawberry row has 7 squares. Count in 10s: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70. So it is 70 children.

items.q: How many red cars went past?
items.e: Look at the key: each square = 2 cars, so half a square = 1. The Red row has 1 square and half a square. Count in 2s: 2, then 1 more for the half. So it is 3 cars.

items.q: Which colour is the most popular?
items.e: Look at the key: each circle = 5 children. The Green row has the most circles: 7 circles. Count in 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35. So it is 35 children.

items.q: Each star stands for 2 children. 7 children chose mint. What goes in the Mint row?
items.e: Count in 2s: 2, 4, 6. That is 3 stars, which makes 6. 1 more is half of 2, so add half a star. Draw 3 and a half stars.

items.q: Which fruit is the least popular?
items.e: Look at the key: each square = 10 children. The Banana row has the fewest squares: 1 square. Count in 10s: 10. So it is 10 children.
Look at the key: each heart = 5 children. Football: 7 hearts = 35. Hopscotch: 4 hearts = 20. How many more means subtract: 35 − 20 = 15.

items.q: How many more children come by scooter than come by bus?
items.e: Look at the key: each circle = 10 children. Scooter: 4 circles = 40. Bus: 2 circles = 20. How many more means subtract: 40 − 20 = 20.

items.q: How many pigeons and blackbirds were seen altogether?
items.e: Look at the key: each square = 2 birds, so half a square = 1. Pigeon: 11. Blackbird: 16. Altogether means add: 11 + 16 = 27.

items.q: How many children chose green or red?
items.e: Look at the key: each square = 10 children. Green: 70. Red: 60. Altogether means add: 70 + 60 = 130.
Look at the key: each heart = 5 children. Car: 3 hearts = 15. Bus: 1 heart = 5. How many fewer means subtract: 15 − 5 = 10.

items.q: How many children chose pears?
items.e: Each block = 1 child. Count the blocks in the Pear column: 12. The top of the column is at 12 on the scale.

items.q: How many blue tits were seen?
items.e: Each block = 1 bird. Count the blocks in the Blue tit column: 6. The top of the column is at 6 on the scale.

items.q: How many days were sunny?
items.e: Each block = 1 day. Count the blocks in the Sunny column: 2. The top of the column is at 2 on the scale.

items.q: Which column shows 9 minibeasts?
items.e: Each block = 1 minibeast. The Spider column has 9 blocks.

items.q: Which flavour is the most popular?
items.e: Each block = 1 child. The tallest column is Strawberry: 12.

items.q: Which way do the fewest children come to school?
items.e: Each block = 1 child. The shortest column is Bike: 2.

items.q: How many more children have a hamster than a rabbit?
items.e: Each block = 1 child. Hamster: 6. Rabbit: 3. How many more means find the difference: 6 − 3 = 3.

items.q: How many fewer silver cars than white cars went past?
items.e: Each block = 1 car. White: 5. Silver: 2. How many fewer means find the difference: 5 − 2 = 3.

items.q: Put the games in order from most to fewest.
items.e: Read each one: Skipping 7, Football 11, Hopscotch 2, Tag 3. Biggest first: Football (11), Skipping (7), Tag (3), Hopscotch (2).

items.q: Put the colours in order from fewest to most.
items.e: Read each one: Yellow 3, Blue 12, Purple 7, Green 5. Smallest first: Yellow (3), Green (5), Purple (7), Blue (12).

items.q: How many children chose skipping?
items.e: Find the Skipping row, then read the number next to it: 15 children.

items.q: How many children chose green?
items.e: Find the Green row, then read the number next to it: 17 children.

items.q: Which bird was seen the most?
items.e: Read the table. The biggest number is Robin: 16.

items.q: Put the fruits in order from most to fewest.
items.e: Read each one: Apple 16, Orange 2, Banana 11, Pear 10. Biggest first: Apple (16), Banana (11), Pear (10), Orange (2).

items.q: How many cars went past altogether?
items.e: Read the table. Add all the numbers: 17 + 5 + 16 + 19 = 57.

items.q: How many more children come by car than walk to school?
items.e: Read the table. Car: 15. Walk: 7. How many more means find the difference: 15 − 7 = 8.

items.q: How many children from Class 2B go to Choir?
items.e: Find the Choir row, then go across to the Class 2B column: 13. (6 is the Class 2A column.)

items.q: How many children go to Football altogether?
items.e: Football row: Class 2A 9, Class 2B 12. Altogether means add: 9 + 12 = 21.

items.q: Which pet do the fewest children have?
items.e: Read the table. The smallest number is Fish: 5.

items.q: Put the flavours in order from fewest to most.
items.e: Read each one: Chocolate 3, Strawberry 18, Vanilla 16, Mint 15. Smallest first: Chocolate (3), Mint (15), Vanilla (16), Strawberry (18).

items.q: How many pupils chose popcorn?
items.e: Each circle stands for 1. Count the circles in the Popcorn row: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6. So the answer is 6 pupils.
Each star stands for 1. Count the stars in the Bus row: 1, 2. So the answer is 2 pupils.

items.q: How many mango scoops were sold?
items.e: Each square stands for 1. Count the squares in the Mango row: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6. So the answer is 6 scoops.
Each heart stands for 1. Count the hearts in the Swim row: 1, 2, 3, 4. So the answer is 4 pupils.

items.q: How many stickers does Kayode have?
items.e: Each circle stands for 1. Count the circles in the Kayode row. There are 8. So the answer is 8 stickers.
Each star stands for 1. Count the stars in the Bee row: 1, 2, 3. So the answer is 3 bugs.

items.q: How many pupils chose spaghetti?
items.e: Each square stands for 1. Count the squares in the Spaghetti row: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6. So the answer is 6 pupils.
Each heart stands for 1. Count the hearts in the Dolls row: 1, 2. So the answer is 2 toys.

items.q: How many pupils have a bird?
items.e: Each circle stands for 1. Count the circles in the Bird row: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6. So the answer is 6 pupils.
Each star stands for 1. Count the stars in the Blue row: 1, 2, 3. So the answer is 3 votes.

items.q: Which row shows the most birds?
items.e: Each square is 1, so the row with the most squares wins. Crow has 7. The others have 4, 6, 3.
Each heart is 1, so the row with the fewest hearts wins. Rainy has 1. The others have 2, 5, 6.

items.q: Which row shows 7 shells?
items.e: Look for a row with 7 circles. Count the circles in the Chidi row. There are 7.
Each star is 1, so the row with the most stars wins. Bisi has 7. The others have 4, 6, 3.
Look for a row with 7 hearts. Count the hearts in the Grape row. There are 7.

items.q: How many shells did Uju find?
items.e: A group of 4 marks with a line across is 5. The Uju row has 1 group of 5 and 1 more mark. 5 + 1 = 6.

items.q: How many votes did Apple get?
items.e: A group of 4 marks with a line across is 5. The Apple row has 1 group of 5 and 3 more marks. 5 + 3 = 8.

items.q: How many ants did the class see?
items.e: A group of 4 marks with a line across is 5. The Ant row has 2 groups of 5 and 3 more marks. 5 + 5 + 3 = 13.

items.q: Which row shows the most pupils?
items.e: Find the row with the most marks. The Pretzels row has 2 groups of 5 and 3 more marks. 5 + 5 + 3 = 13. The other rows are Popcorn 7, Yogurt 10, Grapes 11.

items.q: How many votes did Pear get?
items.e: Each circle stands for 1. Count the circles in the Pear row: 1, 2, 3. So the answer is 3 votes.
